deliberation: The remedy is proportionate: repeated repository operations after one substantive authorization spend scarce volunteer attention on mechanics rather than judgment. Stage 1 is reversible, shadow mode constrains risk, and governed-payload identity addresses churn. Approval is conditional because baseline burden, durable ownership, initial scope, service expectations, promotion thresholds, kill-switch operation, and maintenance-value review are not yet specified. Council Steward advice is not reserved Human Steward disposition.
discharged_obligations: Compared alternatives for volunteer effort, delay, risk, and institutional purpose.
Assessed proportionality, maintainability, reversibility, resource commitment, and scope control.
Distinguished Council Steward advice from Human Steward authority.
findings: Bounded deterministic projection is a better use of volunteer attention than repeated mechanical merges.
The staged rollout is proportionate and substantially reversible.
The burden claim lacks a recorded baseline and target.
Long-term ownership and operating cost are unspecified.
The initial allowlist and expansion rule must remain narrow.
conditions: Record baseline human actions, elapsed time, PR count, polling, retries, and operator minutes.
Require one or fewer Steward actions, zero manual SHA transcription, and at least 70 percent median post-authorization time reduction.
Name the initial repositories, transitions, and paths; separately review any expansion.
Assign a maintainer, backup, incident route, dependency policy, cost ceiling, and quarterly review.
Provide a one-action kill switch and reassess maintenance value after two clean campaigns and after 90 days.
residual_uncertainty: Campaign telemetry, CI cost, maintenance cost, and initial scope are unknown.
The availability and burden of maintainers are unknown.
